title: Utilizing mollusk soft tissue and shells as biomarkers for monitoring heavy metal pollution
author: Krishnan, Saion, et al.

steps.title: Collect specimens and sediment
steps.instruction: Select the five intertidal stations listed in Table 1 along the northern west coast of Peninsular Malaysia; at each station collect approximately 40 Cerithidea obtusa specimens (≈5 cm length) and four surface sediment samples from the top layer using a clean plastic spoon, plus sub‑surface sediment (~5 cm depth, 500–600 g). Place shells, soft tissues, and each sediment sample in separate polyethylene bags, keep them in an ice box, and transport to the laboratory.

steps.title: Store samples frozen
steps.instruction: Store all collected samples at –20 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Thaw and separate tissues
steps.instruction: Partially thaw frozen C. obtusa specimens at room temperature on paper towels, then carefully separate the soft tissue from the shell.

steps.title: Dry samples
steps.instruction: Place sediment, soft tissue, and shell samples in a drying oven set to 80 °C for 72 h or until a constant dry weight is reached.

steps.title: Grind and sieve
steps.instruction: Powder the dried samples with a glass mortar, sieve the powder through a mesh with particle size ≤200 µm, and store the sieved material in polyethylene pillboxes.

steps.title: Weigh and irradiate for INAA
steps.instruction: For each sample weigh ~150 mg for short‑irradiation experiments and ~200 mg for long‑irradiation; perform four replicate experiments per sample. Use the certified multi‑element comparator IAEA‑Soil‑7 for calibration. Irradiate in the MINT TRIGA Mark II reactor (750 kW, thermal neutron flux 3–4 × 10^12 n cm⁻² s⁻¹) via pneumatic transport. Calibrate the gamma‑spectroscopy system with point sources 133Ba, 60Co, 57Co, 137Cs, 54Mn, 241Am (60 keV–2 MeV). For short irradiation expose samples for 1 min; after cooling 20 min count for 5 min and after cooling 24 h count for 20 min. For long irradiation expose for 6 h; after cooling 3–4 days count for 1 h and after cooling 21–28 days count for 1 h. Keep the sample‑detector distance at 12–15 cm for short‑irradiation and 1–2 cm for long‑irradiation; ensure dead time remains below 10 %.

steps.title: Calculate concentrations from INAA
steps.instruction: Determine elemental concentrations on a dry‑weight basis using the comparative equation: C_sam = (A_sam / A_std) × (W_std / W_sam) × C_std, where A = net peak count, W = weight, and C = known concentration of the standard.

steps.title: Digest samples for AAS
steps.instruction: Weigh 1 g of each dried sample, place it in a hot‑block digester, add concentrated HNO₃ (AnalaR grade, BDH 69%). Digest at 40 °C for 1 h, then raise to 140 °C for a minimum of 3 h. Dilute the digest with distilled deionized water, filter through Whatman No. 1 filter paper, and analyse Cd, Cu, Ni, and Pb by atomic absorption spectrophotometry. Express results in mg kg⁻¹ dry weight.

steps.title: Perform statistical analyses
steps.instruction: Import all data into SPSS for Windows (Version 15). Apply a log₁₀(mean + 1) transformation to each variable. Compute Pearson correlation coefficients between Ni, Cd, Fe, Cu, Pb levels in sediment and snail shell/soft tissue, and conduct multiple linear stepwise regression (MLSRA).

steps.title: Compute coefficient of variation
steps.instruction: Using the untransformed data, calculate CV (%) = (standard deviation / mean) × 100 for each measured parameter.

steps.title: Calculate bioaccumulation factor
steps.instruction: Determine BSAF (%) = (mean concentration in tissue / mean concentration in associated sediment) × 100.

steps.title: Classify BSAF values
steps.instruction: Interpret BSAF according to Dallinger: values <1 indicate deconcentrators, 1–2 indicate microconcentrators, and >2 indicate macroconcentrators.
